frontier.hypothesis: With priority and class now measured out, the residual is decided solely by INSN_LUID, and the a2 base insn (211/316) must out-LUID the call's argument setup (240/242, 346/348) to win. Statement order cannot do that (s6 class kill, sched.c:2464), but INSN BIRTH POSITION is a different input: an insn created by a LATER pass is placed at that pass's insertion point, not at its source statement's. combine.c places a combined insn at i3's position, so a source form in which 'addiu a2, s4, -K' is MANUFACTURED by combine at an insn position after the argument setup would carry a LUID above 42 without any statement move.
frontier.mechanism: sched1's INSN_LUIDs are assigned by a linear walk of the insn chain as it stands after flow.c, i.e. after cse/loop/combine have moved and re-created insns. Every session so far has treated the a2 base insn's chain position as fixed by its source statement; it is fixed only for insns that survive from RTL expansion unchanged. The s7 dumps show 211 already present in .flow with the same uid it has in .rtl, i.e. our spelling produces it at expansion — the untested question is whether any spelling produces it downstream instead.
frontier.next_probe: Diff tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s7/dumps2/text1b.rtl against .combine for the block-6 region to enumerate which insns combine CREATES and where it places them; then sweep source forms whose a2 base is only materialised late (e.g. the base folded into an expression that combine must re-split, or the constant -K carried on the store's address arithmetic and re-hoisted). Score with tools/sweep_variants.py and confirm the multiset stays at 176 before crediting anything.

frontier.hypothesis: The a2 base insn's priority would exceed the argument setup's if it were a data consumer of a LOAD (insn_cost 2, sched.c:1497), which is the only mechanism in the pass that produces a priority above the enclosing call's. The cost of forcing that in ordinary C — letting r4 live in memory across the loop instead of a callee-saved register — has never been measured.
frontier.mechanism: insn_cost returns result_ready_cost of the predecessor; only the movsi load pattern yields 2 in this window (measured: 'insn=206 pred=205 kind=0 pred_pri=3 cost=2 contrib=4'). If the base's operand arrived from a load inside the loop, the base insn's priority would be call_priority + 1 and it would win criterion 1 outright, with no LUID involvement at all.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep forms that force r4 (and/or r5) to be re-read inside the loop rather than hoisted — a file-scope or struct-member spelling of the two random bases, and an aliased read that loop.c's invariant_p rejects — and record the instruction-count cost. The prediction is that the rotation flips while the multiset grows; measuring HOW MUCH it grows tells the next session whether any spelling can pay for it.

frontier.hypothesis: s6's statement-permutation kill covered only the eight half-1 statements and explicitly held the loop-top and half-2 statements fixed, but sched1's LUIDs for block 6 are one linear numbering over the whole loop body, so loop-top and half-2 placements shift the LUIDs the tie-break reads.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c:2464 compares absolute INSN_LUIDs, and every insn in block 6 shares one numbering. Moving statements outside the half-1 window changes the LUID gap between 211 and 240/242 only if it changes how many insns are born between them — which the loop-top statements cannot do, but a cross-half move (computing half 2's p0/p1 setup before half 1's call) can.
frontier.next_probe: Extend tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s6/compose.py's permutation space to the loop-top and half-2 statements (its current 420-permutation space deliberately fixed them), express the goal on sched1's OUTPUT position of 211 rather than on the final order, and cross-check any model hit with tools/sweep_variants.py before crediting it.
